$comment: Generated by `make docs-gen` from deploy/helm/myriarch/values.schema.source.yaml and internal/config. Do not edit this file by hand: change the source or the configuration structure and run `make docs-gen`.
title: Values of the myriarch chart
description: Values of the Helm chart myriarch, which runs the myriarch server (myriarchd). The schema is strict: helm install, upgrade, template and lint refuse a key that the chart does not know, a value of the wrong type and a malformed value. The block config mirrors the configuration file of the server and is generated from the configuration structure. Secrets are not values: the chart reads them from Kubernetes Secrets.

replicaCount.description: Number of myriarchd replicas. All replicas serve agents and the API; the singleton jobs run on the leader.

registry.description: Registry host, with an optional port, of the image, for example ghcr.io. It applies when image.repository has no registry host of its own, and global.imageRegistry takes precedence over it. Empty means the default registry of the container runtime.

repository.description: Repository of the image without a registry host, for example myriarch/myriarch. A repository that starts with a registry host (registry.example.com/myriarch/myriarch, the form of the values of v0.1.0) is used unchanged and neither image.registry nor global.imageRegistry applies. The first segment is a registry host when it contains a . or a : or is localhost, as for the container runtimes; otherwise it belongs to the repository, which is in lower case.

tag.description: Image tag. Empty means the appVersion of the chart.

digest.description: Image digest, sha256: followed by 64 hexadecimal characters. When set, the image is referenced as repository@digest and the tag is ignored.

imagePullSecrets.description: Secrets for pulling the image from a private registry.

name.description: Name of the Secret in the release namespace.

nameOverride.description: Overrides the chart name in resource names.

global.description: Values that a parent chart shares with its subcharts. This chart reads only global.imageRegistry; other keys belong to other charts and are not checked.

imageRegistry.description: Registry host, with an optional port, that replaces image.registry, for example the host of a mirror. A repository that has a registry host of its own is not affected. A parent chart may pass null for no mirror.

enabled.description: Read by the dependency condition of a parent chart (condition: myriarch.enabled), not by this chart, which ignores it. It has no default and no effect on a standalone installation.

serviceAccount.description: The ServiceAccount of the pods. It has no API access, because its token is not mounted.

name.description: Name of the ServiceAccount. Empty means a name generated from the release name.

config.description: The configuration file of the server (myriarchd.yaml), which the chart renders into a ConfigMap. Keys, types and descriptions come from the configuration structure and are the ones of docs/reference/configuration.md; a default that a description names is the default of the server, the defaults of the chart are in values.yaml. The chart does not offer these keys: auth.bootstrapAdmin (use the top-level bootstrapAdmin values), opamp.enrollmentTokens (use the top-level enrollmentTokens values), auth.devLogin (the chart never starts the development mode), dev (the chart never starts the development mode), database.dsn (a secret, use database.dsnFile), auth.oidc.clientSecret (a secret, use auth.oidc.clientSecretFile), gitops.webhookSecret (a secret, use gitops.webhookSecretFile), notifications.channels[].url (a secret, use notifications.channels[].urlFile).

server.description: `server` configures the main HTTP listener (UI, REST API, OpAMP).

listenAddr.description: `listenAddr` is the address of the main HTTP listener, as host:port or :port (default ":8080").

publicUrl.description: `publicUrl` is the externally reachable base URL (used for OIDC redirects, artifact download URLs, notification links), e.g. "https://fleet.example.com". Required in production.

tls.description: `tls` configures server-side TLS. If `server.tls.certFile` and `server.tls.keyFile` are set, myriarchd terminates TLS itself; otherwise TLS terminates at the ingress and `server.tls.terminatedUpstream` must be set explicitly in production.

certFile.description: `certFile` is the PEM file with the server certificate. Set it together with `server.tls.keyFile`; with both set, myriarchd terminates TLS itself.

keyFile.description: `keyFile` is the PEM file with the private key of the server certificate. Set it together with `server.tls.certFile`.

clientCaFile.description: `clientCaFile` enables (optional) client certificate verification for the OpAMP endpoint (mTLS). Clients without certificate are still accepted if `opamp.requireClientCert` is false.

terminatedUpstream.description: `terminatedUpstream` declares that TLS is terminated in front of myriarchd (ingress, load balancer) and that the plaintext listener is only reachable from there. Production refuses to start with a plaintext listener unless this is set (the Helm chart sets it); myriarchd logs a warning at startup.

trustedProxies.description: `trustedProxies` lists the proxies (CIDRs) whose X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Client-Cert headers are honored.

metricsListenAddr.description: `metricsListenAddr` is the address of a separate listener that serves /metrics (default ":9090"; empty = serve /metrics on `server.listenAddr`).

path.description: `path` is the URL path of the OpAMP endpoint (default "/v1/opamp").

requireEnrollmentToken.description: `requireEnrollmentToken` rejects connections without a valid "Authorization: Bearer myre_..." header (default true; dev mode false).

requireClientCert.description: `requireClientCert` rejects connections without a verified client certificate (mTLS, either terminated by myriarchd or forwarded by a trusted proxy).

clientCertHeader.description: `clientCertHeader` is the header that carries the URL-encoded PEM client certificate from a trusted proxy (e.g. "X-Forwarded-Client-Cert" or "ssl-client-cert").

offlineAfter.description: `offlineAfter` marks an agent offline when it sent no message for this long (default 90s = 3 x the supervisor default heartbeat of 30s).

staleApplyingAfter.description: `staleApplyingAfter` is how long one connection of an agent may keep reporting APPLYING for the desired config, unchanged, before the server offers the config once more (once per connection; default 90s, 3 x the supervisor default heartbeat of 30s; 0 turns it off). A supervisor that restarts while it applies a config reports the stored APPLYING again after it reconnects, and nothing ends it; without this setting a rollout waits for the `applyTimeout` of its policy. The time counts from the first report on the connection, so short connections never cause an offer. Keep it above the `config_apply_timeout` of the supervisors (30s in the shipped templates) and below the `applyTimeout` of the rollout policies (10 minutes for configuration by default).

lastSeenFlushInterval.description: `lastSeenFlushInterval` is the batch interval for the `last_seen_at` writes (default 15s).

maxMessageSize.description: `maxMessageSize` is the largest accepted OpAMP message in bytes (default 4 MiB; the default of the OpAMP library is 64 MiB).

autoRebindOnTokenRotation.description: `autoRebindOnTokenRotation` lets an agent whose bound enrollment token was revoked or expired move to another valid token (same client certificate subject) without an admin action; the move is audited as agent.rebind (default false: `POST /agents/{id}/actions/reenroll` is required).

maxEffectiveConfigBytes.description: `maxEffectiveConfigBytes` limits the effective config body of one agent that is stored (default 1 MiB); larger bodies are not stored and produce a warning event for the agent.

enableCompression.description: `enableCompression` turns on WebSocket permessage-deflate (default false). The read limit of the WebSocket library applies to the compressed frame only, so decompressed messages would not be bounded by `opamp.maxMessageSize`; enable it only if that is acceptable. Production refuses it unless `opamp.allowUnboundedCompression` acknowledges the risk.

allowUnboundedCompression.description: `allowUnboundedCompression` acknowledges that decompressed WebSocket messages are not bounded by `opamp.maxMessageSize` (default false). Only consulted in production, where `opamp.enableCompression` requires it.

sendTimeout.description: `sendTimeout` is the write deadline for pushing a message to one agent (default 10s). The send call of the OpAMP library ignores context cancellation, therefore the server sets the deadline on the underlying network connection.

maxConnectionsPerReplica.description: `maxConnectionsPerReplica` limits the OpAMP connections of one replica: above it, new connections get 503 with Retry-After (default 10000).

connectRateLimit.description: `connectRateLimit` limits authenticated new connections per second per replica (token bucket, burst = 2x; default 200). Excess gets 429 + Retry-After. The bucket is charged after authentication, so unauthenticated requests cannot exhaust it.

connectRatePerIp.description: `connectRatePerIp` limits connection attempts per second and client IP (token bucket, burst = 2x; default 50; 0 = default). Behind a proxy the client IP is only known if `server.trustedProxies` lists the proxy; otherwise all agents share the proxy address.

maxConnectionsPerToken.description: `maxConnectionsPerToken` limits concurrent WebSocket connections per enrollment token and replica (default 0 = unlimited).

dsnFile.description: `dsnFile` reads the DSN from a file (takes precedence over `database.dsn`).

maxConns.description: `maxConns` is the maximum size of the connection pool (default 20).

migrateOnStart.description: `migrateOnStart` runs pending migrations at startup (default true). Migrations take a Postgres advisory lock, so concurrent replicas are safe. When it is false and the schema lacks migrations of this version, myriarchd refuses to start: run `myriarchd migrate` first. A schema that is newer than this version but compatible with it starts with a warning, and a schema that is incompatible with it is refused, whatever this setting says.

statementTimeout.description: `statementTimeout` is the server-side limit of one SQL statement of the application pool (default 15s; migrations and housekeeping are exempt).

oidc.description: `oidc` configures single sign-on with an OpenID Connect identity provider.

enabled.description: `enabled` turns on single sign-on through OpenID Connect (default false).

issuerUrl.description: `issuerUrl` is the issuer of the identity provider exactly as its discovery document states it, e.g. "https://idp.example.com/realms/otel" (no trailing slash). Some providers need a specific form, which myriarchd checks when it loads the configuration.

clientId.description: `clientId` is the client identifier that is registered for myriarchd at the identity provider.

clientSecretFile.description: `clientSecretFile` reads the client secret from a file (takes precedence over `auth.oidc.clientSecret`; read only while `auth.oidc.enabled` is true).

clientCertificateFile.description: `clientCertificateFile` authenticates the client with a certificate instead of a secret (`private_key_jwt`, for providers that register a client certificate): the PEM certificate of the client registration. Set it together with `auth.oidc.clientKeyFile`; it excludes `auth.oidc.clientSecret` and `auth.oidc.clientSecretFile`. The file is read again when it changes.

clientKeyFile.description: `clientKeyFile` is the RSA private key (PKCS#1 or PKCS#8, PEM) that belongs to `auth.oidc.clientCertificateFile`. Set both or none. The file is read again when it changes.

scopes.description: `scopes` are the OAuth scopes that myriarchd requests at login; the list must contain "openid" (default: openid, profile, email).

groupsClaim.description: `groupsClaim` is the claim that holds the groups of the user (default "groups"). The claim may hold a string, a list of strings or an object (its keys count); a dotted path reaches into nested objects.

nameClaim.description: `nameClaim` is the claim that holds the display name (default "name"; "preferred_username" is the fallback when it is empty).

emailClaim.description: `emailClaim` is the claim that holds the e-mail address (default "email"). "email:" entries of `auth.oidc.roleMapping.users` require the default: `email_verified` attests only the standard claim.

roleMapping.description: `roleMapping` maps groups (or roles) and individual users to roles; the highest role wins.

admin.description: `admin` lists the groups (or roles) whose members get the admin role.

operator.description: `operator` lists the groups (or roles) whose members get the operator role.

viewer.description: `viewer` lists the groups (or roles) whose members get the viewer role.

users.description: `users` maps individual users to roles, for identity providers without a groups claim.

admin.description: `admin` lists the users who get the admin role.

operator.description: `operator` lists the users who get the operator role.

viewer.description: `viewer` lists the users who get the viewer role.

defaultRole.description: `defaultRole` is the role of users without a matching group. Default "" = deny (`access_denied`, audited). Only set it deliberately (e.g. "viewer" when every user of the IdP application may read); myriarchd logs a warning.

displayName.description: `displayName` is shown on the login button (e.g. "Company SSO").

sessionTtl.description: `sessionTtl` is the idle timeout of a session (default 2h), sliding.

sessionMaxAge.description: `sessionMaxAge` is the absolute lifetime of a session, independent of activity (default 12h). After it users sign in again, so identity provider changes (groups, disabled accounts) take effect.

apiTokenMaxTtl.description: `apiTokenMaxTtl` is the maximum lifetime of API tokens (default 90 days): a token created without expiresAt gets it, a longer expiresAt is refused, and an older token stops working. 0 means unlimited (production logs a warning). It is the only way a removal at the identity provider reaches API tokens besides disabling the user in Myriarch.

cookieSecure.description: `cookieSecure` forces the Secure cookie flag (default true; dev false). With it the session cookie is named __Host-myriarch_session.

downloadTokenSecretFile.description: `downloadTokenSecretFile` is the file with the HMAC key for artifact download tokens (32+ random bytes). The key is generated and stored in the KV store if this is empty. Tokens: see `artifacts.downloadTokenTtl`.

enabled.description: `enabled` turns the GitOps syncer on (default true).

repoUrl.description: `repoUrl` is the repository: https://..., ssh://git@..., git@host:org/repo.git or "dir:///abs/path" / "dir:relative/path" for a plain directory (dev, tests; revision = content hash).

branch.description: `branch` is the branch that myriarchd follows (default "main").

path.description: `path` is the directory inside the repository that holds the GitOps files (default "" = root).

auth.description: `auth` holds the credentials for the repository.

username.description: `username` is the user name for HTTPS, used together with `gitops.auth.tokenFile` (GitLab: username "oauth2" or any).

tokenFile.description: `tokenFile` is the file with the access token for HTTPS, used together with `gitops.auth.username`.

sshKeyFile.description: `sshKeyFile` is the private key file for ssh repositories.

knownHostsFile.description: `knownHostsFile` is the known_hosts file for ssh repositories. It is required for them: host key verification is mandatory.

caFile.description: `caFile` is a PEM file with the CA certificate of a self-signed Git server.

pollInterval.description: `pollInterval` is how often the repository is fetched (default 60s).

webhookSecretFile.description: `webhookSecretFile` reads the webhook secret from a file (takes precedence over `gitops.webhookSecret`; read only while `gitops.enabled` is true).

maxRepoBytes.description: `maxRepoBytes` limits the size of the checked-out repository (default 256 MiB).

maxFiles.description: `maxFiles` limits the number of YAML files in the repository (default 2000).

maxYamlBytes.description: `maxYamlBytes` limits the total size of the YAML files (default 64 MiB).

cloneDir.description: `cloneDir` is the directory of the local clone. Default: a directory in the temporary directory, named after the repository URL; production setups set a directory that only the server account can write (a warning names an empty value).

uiRepoWebUrl.description: `uiRepoWebUrl` builds the "view in Git" links, e.g. "https://gitlab.example.com/otel/fleet-config/-/blob/{commit}/{path}".

enabled.description: `enabled` turns the release tracker on (default true).

githubApiUrl.description: `githubApiUrl` is the GitHub API that is polled for releases (default "https://api.github.com"; GitHub Enterprise: "https://ghe.example.com/api/v3").

rawBaseUrl.description: `rawBaseUrl` is the base URL for the CHANGELOG files (default "https://raw.githubusercontent.com"; GHES: "https://ghe.example.com/raw").

tokenFile.description: `tokenFile` is a file with a GitHub token (raises the rate limit from 60 to 5000/h).

releasesRepo.description: `releasesRepo` is the repository of the collector distributions (default "open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases").

coreRepo.description: `coreRepo` is the repository of the collector core (default "open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector").

contribRepo.description: `contribRepo` is the repository of the collector contrib components (default "open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib").

pollInterval.description: `pollInterval` is how often the upstream releases are polled (default 1h).

minVersion.description: `minVersion` ignores older releases on the first import (default "0.120.0").

fixtureDir.description: `fixtureDir` reads releases and changelogs from recorded files instead of the network (tests, offline dev).

dir.description: `dir` is the directory for cached files, per replica. Default: a fixed directory in the temporary directory; production setups set a directory that only the server account can write (a warning names an empty value).

sourceBaseUrl.description: `sourceBaseUrl` is where release assets are fetched from. Default "https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/releases/download". An internal mirror must use the same layout: `<base>/<tag>/<asset>`.

agentBaseUrls.description: `agentBaseUrls` is an allowlist of base URLs updaters download from ("http://myriarchd:8080"): absolute http(s) URLs without path, query, fragment or credentials. For every package offer myriarchd picks, per updater, the entry whose host:port equals the host:port of the attribute dev.myriarch.updater.server_endpoint the updater reported (the OpAMP endpoint it is connected to); updaters without a match download from `server.publicUrl`. This lets agents inside a cluster use an internal service name while agents elsewhere keep the public route. http:// entries need `artifacts.allowInsecureAgentBaseUrls` in production.

allowInsecureAgentBaseUrls.description: `allowInsecureAgentBaseUrls` permits http:// entries in `artifacts.agentBaseUrls` in production (a cluster-internal service whose traffic never leaves the namespace); myriarchd logs a warning. Package contents are verified by SHA-256 and sigstore on the updater in any case.

prefetchPlatforms.description: `prefetchPlatforms` lists the platforms to prefetch on new target versions, e.g. ["linux/amd64", "windows/amd64"]. Default: empty. Member platforms of updater fleets are always added; an explicit prefetch request that names no platforms falls back to the platforms of the connected collectors that use the requested distribution.

verify.description: `verify` configures the verification of upstream artifacts.

requireChecksum.description: `requireChecksum` verifies SHA-256 against the per-asset "<asset>.sha256" file (releases >= v0.158.0; older releases: shared checksums.txt) (default true).

requireSignature.description: `requireSignature` verifies the per-asset sigstore bundle "<asset>.sigstore.json" (cosign keyless, Rekor + TSA) (default true).

certificateIdentityRegexp.description: `certificateIdentityRegexp` is the regular expression that the SAN of the Fulcio certificate must match. The default accepts the contrib workflow (base-release.yaml) and the supervisor workflow (base-binary-release.yaml) of the upstream release repository for plain vX.Y.Z tags. Additionally the verifier requires the tag to equal the artifact version.

certificateOidcIssuer.description: `certificateOidcIssuer` is the OIDC issuer of the Fulcio certificate (default "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com").

trustedRootFile.description: `trustedRootFile` is the sigstore trusted_root.json for offline verification; empty = fetch via TUF from the public Sigstore instance.

tufRepositoryUrl.description: `tufRepositoryUrl` is the base URL of the Sigstore TUF repository or of a 1:1 mirror of it (default "" = https://tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev); the embedded Sigstore root remains the trust anchor. Ignored if `artifacts.verify.trustedRootFile` is set. TUF requests use the same HTTP client as the other outbound connections (proxy environment, `outbound.caFile`, `outbound.allowedCidrs`, `artifacts.sourceAuth` for the origin of `artifacts.sourceBaseUrl`). A mirror must not cache timestamp.json for long (it changes daily).

maxCacheBytes.description: `maxCacheBytes` limits the size of the cache (default 20 GiB); least recently used versions are evicted.

downloadTokenTtl.description: `downloadTokenTtl` limits the age of updater download tokens (default 24h; 0 = no expiry). A token (bound to artifact id and updater agent id) is accepted only while that agent has a package offer referencing the artifact; the offer is re-sent with a fresh token once the token is older than half of the TTL.

sourceAuth.description: `sourceAuth` are the credentials myriarchd sends to the artifact mirror (`artifacts.sourceBaseUrl`), e.g. an Artifactory access token or a Nexus user. They are sent ONLY to requests with the same origin (scheme, host, port) as `artifacts.sourceBaseUrl`, never to redirect targets on other hosts. Hosts that download from the mirror themselves are not affected.

username.description: `username` is the user for basic authentication (Nexus); only together with `artifacts.sourceAuth.passwordFile`.

passwordFile.description: `passwordFile` holds the password or user token for basic authentication.

tokenFile.description: `tokenFile` holds a bearer token (Artifactory access token). It excludes `artifacts.sourceAuth.username` and `artifacts.sourceAuth.passwordFile`.

proxyUrl.description: `proxyUrl` is the forward proxy for outbound downloads (optional).

allowedRedirectHosts.description: `allowedRedirectHosts` lists the hosts upstream downloads may be redirected to (exact or `*.suffix`; https only, at most 5 hops). Default: the GitHub release asset hosts plus the host of `artifacts.sourceBaseUrl`.

allowUnverified.description: `allowUnverified` permits `artifacts.verify.requireChecksum` = false or `artifacts.verify.requireSignature` = false in production (lab use only).

install.description: `install` configures the installation of hosts from the server (ADR-0046): the plan that a host asks for with its enrollment token, the install grants for its downloads, the installer bundles of the release that the server runs and the rendered install commands.

enabled.description: `enabled` turns the installation of hosts from the server on (default true). When it is off, every route under `/install` answers 404 and the server fetches no installer bundle.

grantTtl.description: `grantTtl` is the lifetime of an install grant, the credential with which a host downloads the collector and the supervisor after it asked for its plan (default 1h; when neither the file nor the environment sets it, it is `artifacts.downloadTokenTtl` if that is shorter). A grant is also bound to the enrollment token of that request and stops working when the token is revoked or expires. In production the value must be positive and at most `artifacts.downloadTokenTtl`.

bundleSourceBaseUrl.description: `bundleSourceBaseUrl` is where the installer bundles of the release that the server runs come from (default "https://github.com/myriarch/myriarch/releases/download"). A mirror keeps the layout `<base>/v<version>/<asset>` with `checksums.txt` and its Sigstore bundle `checksums.txt.sigstore.json` next to the archives; the server verifies both against the identity of the release workflow, whichever server they come from. Production requires https. The value must not be empty while `install.enabled` is on.

platforms.description: `platforms` lists the platforms that a host can be installed on from the server, as "os/arch" (default linux/amd64, linux/arm64 and windows/amd64, which is all that is supported). The plan refuses a host on another platform, and the server prepares an installer bundle for each platform listed.

outbound.description: `outbound` is the destination policy of all outbound connections.

allowedCidrs.description: `allowedCidrs` opens address ranges (or single IPs) that are denied by default: loopback, private (RFC 1918), shared, link-local (metadata), unique-local and reserved ranges. Example: ["10.20.0.0/16"] for an AWX server or Git server in the internal network. Applies to the resolved address of every connection, including redirects.

caFile.description: `caFile` is a PEM file with ADDITIONAL trusted CA certificates (on top of the system roots) for ALL outbound TLS connections of myriarchd: OIDC, Git over HTTPS, GitHub API and raw, the artifact upstream or mirror, the Sigstore TUF repository, webhook and AWX executors, notification channels. Typically the internal CA of the company. myriarchd refuses to start if the file is unreadable or contains no certificate.

allowedWebhookHosts.description: `allowedWebhookHosts` restricts webhook/AWX targets (host, host:port, `*.example.com`; http://host allows plain HTTP). An empty list refuses every webhook and AWX target (fail closed) in every mode; it does not stop startup.

defaultTimeout.description: `defaultTimeout` is the timeout for outbound executor calls (default 30s).

maxTimeout.description: `maxTimeout` caps the timeouts requested by Executor objects in Git (default 5m).

secretEnvPrefix.description: `secretEnvPrefix` is the prefix that environment variables must start with when an Executor object references them directly (secretEnv/tokenEnv; default `MYRIARCH_EXEC_`), so Git cannot read arbitrary variables.

secretDir.description: `secretDir` is the only directory executor secret and CA files (secretFile/tokenFile/caFile) are read from; names must be relative and may not leave it. Empty = file references are refused.

secrets.description: `secrets` is the registry of named secrets. An Executor object may use a registry name as secretEnv/tokenEnv/secretFile/tokenFile value; the secret is then only sent to the listed hosts.

env.description: `env` is the environment variable that holds the secret (or `executors.secrets.<name>.file`).

file.description: `file` is a file below `executors.secretDir` (or an absolute path configured here by the operator).

allowedHosts.description: `allowedHosts` lists the only destinations this secret may be sent to (host, host:port or `*.example.com`). Required.

secretEnvHosts.description: `secretEnvHosts` binds environment variables that are referenced by their prefixed name (secretEnv/tokenEnv) to the only destinations they may be sent to (host, host:port or `*.example.com`). In production an unbound prefixed variable is refused.

secretFileHosts.description: `secretFileHosts` does for files below `executors.secretDir` (secretFile/tokenFile) what `executors.secretEnvHosts` does for environment variables: it binds them, keyed by the relative file name, to the only destinations they may be sent to.

tickInterval.description: `tickInterval` is the interval of the engine loop on the leader (default 5s).

defaultTimezone.description: `defaultTimezone` is the time zone for maintenance windows when an agent has no valid timezone attribute (default "UTC").

autoStart.description: `autoStart` starts rollouts created by GitOps immediately (default true).

executorTimeout.description: `executorTimeout` is the hard limit of one executor call (Start/Cancel of the webhook/AWX/updater executors; default 2m). The engine never waits for a slow executor inside a tick: calls run in the background and their results are applied on a later tick.

channels.description: `channels` lists the notification channels. ${VAR} expansion works inside the entries.

name.description: `name` identifies the channel; unique within the list.

type.description: `type` is the kind of the channel: "webhook", "teams" or "slack".

urlFile.description: `urlFile` reads the URL from a file (takes precedence over `notifications.channels[].url`; always read).

secretFile.description: `secretFile` holds the HMAC secret for type webhook (header X-Myriarch-Signature).

events.description: `events` lists the events routed to this channel, e.g. ["release.new", "rollout.*"]; empty = all.

minSeverity.description: `minSeverity` is the lowest severity routed to this channel: "info" (default), "warning" or "critical".

retention.description: `retention` configures housekeeping (leader job, runs hourly). A value of 0 turns off the cleanup of that kind of data.

agentEvents.description: `agentEvents` is how long agent events are kept (default 30 days).

audit.description: `audit` is how long audit events are kept (default 400 days).

offlineAgents.description: `offlineAgents` is how long an agent may stay offline before housekeeping deletes it (default 30 days; 0 = keep).

finishedRollouts.description: `finishedRollouts` is how long finished rollouts are kept (default 180 days).

unreferencedConfig.description: `unreferencedConfig` is the age after which rendered and effective configurations that nothing references are removed (default 7 days).

gitopsSyncHistory.description: `gitopsSyncHistory` is how long the history of GitOps syncs is kept (default 30 days).

telemetry.description: `telemetry` configures myriarchd's own logs and metrics.

logLevel.description: `logLevel` is the log level: debug, info, warn or error (default info).

logFormat.description: `logFormat` is the log format: json or text (default json; dev text).

replicaId.description: `replicaId` identifies the replica (default: hostname + "-" + random suffix).

leaderLockKey.description: `leaderLockKey` is the Postgres advisory lock key of the leader election (default 7012024).

heartbeatInterval.description: `heartbeatInterval` is the interval of the replica registry heartbeat (default 10s).

ui.description: `ui` configures the language options the web UI receives through the public `GET /auth/config` endpoint.

defaultLanguage.description: `defaultLanguage` is the BCP 47 tag the UI uses when the user has no stored choice and no browser language matches a shipped locale (default "en").

languages.description: `languages` restricts the languages the UI offers (empty = every language the UI ships). When set, it must contain `ui.defaultLanguage`. Entries match a shipped language by the full tag or the primary subtag ("de-DE" enables "de").

oidcFromEnvironment.description: Declares that single sign-on is switched on by environment variables (MYRIARCH_AUTH_OIDC_ENABLED in extraEnv, a ConfigMap or a Secret), which the chart cannot read. The chart then treats OIDC as enabled; the server reads the environment.

bootstrapAdmin.description: The bootstrap admin, a break-glass administrator that works without an identity provider. Its credentials come from a Secret that the chart generates or that bootstrapAdmin.existingSecret names.

username.description: User name of the account, 1 to 64 characters from letters, digits, ".", "_", "@" and "-".

existingSecret.description: Secret that holds the credentials. Empty means that the chart generates the Secret <fullname>-bootstrap with a random one-time token.

tokenKey.description: Key of the one-time token in the Secret. Empty means no token, only a password hash, and needs existingSecret.

passwordHashKey.description: Key of a bcrypt password hash in existingSecret. Needs existingSecret.

keepWithOidc.description: Keep the bootstrap admin active next to single sign-on (break-glass).

enrollmentTokens.description: Enrollment tokens for agents that exist from the first start. A token is never a value: each entry names a Secret that holds it, or the chart generates the Secret with a random token.

name.description: Name of the token, a DNS label, unique in the list. It is also the name of the mounted file.

existingSecret.description: Secret that holds the token. Empty means that the chart generates the Secret <fullname>-enrollment-<name> with a random token.

key.description: Key of the token in the Secret. Empty means token.

labels.description: Labels that agents get when they enroll with the token.

expiresAt.description: Expiry as an RFC 3339 time stamp. Empty means that the token does not expire.

existingSecret.description: Name of the Secret with the files of the server (database-dsn and the optional keys). It is mounted at /etc/myriarchd/secrets.

secretChecksum.description: Roll the pods when a Secret that they mount changes.

enabled.description: Add the annotation checksum/secret to the pods.

secretEnv.description: Environment variables for the executors, each taken from one key of the Secret existingSecret.

name.description: Name of the variable. It must start with config.executors.secretEnvPrefix.

optional.description: Start the pod without the variable when the key is missing.

extraEnv.description: Additional environment variables of the myriarchd container, in the format of a Kubernetes container.

extraVolumes.description: Additional volumes of the pod, in the format of a Kubernetes pod.

extraVolumeMounts.description: Additional volume mounts of the myriarchd container, in the format of a Kubernetes container.

openshift.description: The OpenShift profile: no fixed user, group or fsGroup, a Route instead of an Ingress, the router namespace in the network policy and the OpenShift DNS pods.

enabled.description: true selects the OpenShift profile, false the standard profile, and auto the OpenShift profile when the cluster offers the API security.openshift.io/v1. helm template renders the standard profile for auto unless it gets --api-versions security.openshift.io/v1.

route.description: The Route of the OpenShift profile.

enabled.description: Create the Route in the OpenShift profile.

host.description: Host of the Route. Empty means the host of config.server.publicUrl, without the port.

annotations.description: Further annotations of the Route. The router timeout annotations are always set unless this map sets them.

timeout.description: Router timeout for the long-lived OpAMP WebSockets, a number with a unit (us, ms, s, m, h or d), for example 3600s.

insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy.description: What the router does with plain HTTP requests.

externalCertificateSecret.description: Secret (kubernetes.io/tls, same namespace) with a certificate for the host of the Route. Empty means the default certificate of the router.

routerNamespaceSelector.description: Namespace selector of the router pods, the source of port 8080 while the Route is rendered.

dns.description: Destination of the DNS egress rule in the OpenShift profile.

ports.description: Ports of the DNS service, used for UDP and TCP.

port.description: Port of the HTTP service (UI, REST and OpAMP).

networkPolicy.description: Network segmentation. Port 8080 is reachable from the listed sources only, port 9090 from the monitoring instance, and egress is limited to DNS and the listed ports. A CNI with NetworkPolicy support is a prerequisite.

ingress.description: Sources of port 8080 (UI, REST and OpAMP).

from.description: Sources in NetworkPolicy peer format, for example the namespace of the ingress controller or Gateway. Required while ingress or httpRoute is enabled.

allowSameNamespace.description: Allow every pod of the release namespace to reach port 8080. It must be false while config.server.trustedProxies or config.opamp.clientCertHeader is set.

from.description: Sources in NetworkPolicy peer format. Empty means nobody.

enabled.description: Restrict egress to DNS and the ports below.

ports.description: Allowed destination ports (TCP) for all destinations, by default 5432 for PostgreSQL and 443 for HTTPS. The Git SSH port is added automatically while config.gitops is enabled with an SSH URL.

extraPorts.description: Further ports (TCP), merged into the rule above.

exceptCidrs.description: Destinations that the rule excludes, by default the cloud metadata service.

dns.description: DNS rule of the standard profile. The OpenShift profile uses openshift.dns.

ports.description: Ports of the DNS service, used for UDP and TCP.

extraRules.description: Further egress rules in NetworkPolicy format.

ingress.description: An Ingress, off by default. The Gateway API (httpRoute) is the recommended way; examples for the ingress controllers are in the directory examples of the chart.

className.description: Ingress class. Empty means the default class of the cluster.

annotations.description: Annotations for the controller. OpAMP connections are long-lived WebSockets, so the controller needs long timeouts.

hosts.description: Host names and paths of the Ingress.

tls.description: TLS of the Ingress. Required while config.server.publicUrl is https, unless allowWithoutTls is set.

allowWithoutTls.description: Allow an https publicUrl without ingress.tls, because TLS terminates outside the Ingress.

allowWithoutTrustedProxies.description: Allow an empty config.server.trustedProxies, so that all clients appear with the address of the ingress controller.

httpRoute.description: A Gateway API HTTPRoute, off by default and recommended for new installations. The chart creates the route, not the Gateway. The same checks apply as for the Ingress: trustedProxies and TLS at the Gateway.

parentRefs.description: Gateways that the route is bound to, in the format of the Gateway API. Required while enabled.

hostnames.description: Host names of the route. They must match config.server.publicUrl. Required while enabled.

tlsTerminatedAtGateway.description: Confirms that the Gateway listener terminates TLS. Required with an https publicUrl, because the chart cannot check the Gateway.

timeouts.description: Timeouts of the rule (Gateway API 1.1 and later); support differs per implementation.

resources.description: Resource requests and limits of the myriarchd container. Many clusters require ephemeral-storage. Keep artifacts.maxCacheBytes below emptyDir.sizeLimit, and limits.ephemeral-storage above emptyDir.sizeLimit plus the 256Mi tmp volume plus the logs.

preStopSleepSeconds.description: Pause before the shutdown, so that the endpoint disappears from the load balancers before the connections are closed.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Grace period of the pod on termination.

probes.description: Startup, liveness and readiness probes of the myriarchd container.

startup.description: Startup probe. The container gets failureThreshold times periodSeconds to start before the liveness probe takes over.

liveness.description: Liveness probe. The kubelet restarts the container when it fails.

readiness.description: Readiness probe. A pod that fails it receives no traffic.

tests.description: The Pod of "helm test" (the Helm hook test), which runs "myriarchd healthcheck" against the Service of the release: GET /readyz must answer 200, and a WebSocket upgrade at config.opamp.path must be refused with 401 or, with tests.token, accepted with 101. The Pod sends no OpAMP message and registers no agent. It runs under the restricted Pod Security profile and mounts no Secret unless tests.token names one.

enabled.description: Render the test Pod. The Pod exists only while "helm test" runs. "helm template | kubectl apply" creates it as an ordinary Pod; "helm template --skip-tests" leaves it out.

token.description: Opt-in for the complete OpAMP handshake. The Secret holds an enrollment token that exists for the test only, never the Secret of the agents. The chart refuses the Secrets of the server itself (existingSecret and the bootstrap Secret), and only the key below is mounted, at /etc/myriarchd-test/token.

existingSecret.description: Name of the Secret with the token of the test. Empty means that the Pod mounts no Secret.

key.description: Key of the token in the Secret.

podAnnotations.description: Annotations of the test Pod, for example the opt-out from the sidecar injection of a service mesh. A sidecar that keeps running stops the Pod from completing. The chart sets the annotations of the hook itself, and a key that starts with helm.sh/hook is refused: it would change or, as a null, remove the hook, and the Pod would become an ordinary resource of the release.

resources.description: Resource requests and limits of the test Pod. Many clusters require them, also for ephemeral-storage.

podDisruptionBudget.description: PodDisruptionBudget. It is rendered only while replicaCount is greater than 1, because a budget of 1 on a single replica would block every node drain.

minAvailable.description: Minimum number or percentage of available pods. Ignored while maxUnavailable is set.

maxUnavailable.description: Maximum number or percentage of unavailable pods. It replaces minAvailable when set.

podSecurityContext.description: Security context of the pod, in the format of a Kubernetes pod. The OpenShift profile drops runAsUser, runAsGroup and fsGroup. Other fields are passed through and validated by the API server.

securityContext.description: Security context of the myriarchd container, in the format of a Kubernetes container. Other fields are passed through and validated by the API server.

persistence.description: Data per replica (the GitOps clone and the artifact cache). By default an emptyDir; with persistence.enabled a shared PVC is mounted, and it needs ReadWriteMany while replicaCount is greater than 1.

enabled.description: Mount a PersistentVolumeClaim instead of an emptyDir.

existingClaim.description: Name of an existing claim. Empty means that the chart creates one.

storageClass.description: Storage class of the created claim. Empty means the default class.

accessModes.description: Access modes of the created claim.

emptyDir.description: The volume of the data per replica while persistence is disabled.

sizeLimit.description: Size limit of the emptyDir volume. It must stay above config.artifacts.maxCacheBytes.

topologySpreadConstraints.description: Spreads the replicas, in the format of a Kubernetes pod. The chart adds the label selector of the release to every entry.

affinity.description: Affinity of the pods, in the format of a Kubernetes pod.

serviceMonitor.description: A Prometheus Operator ServiceMonitor. The cluster needs the CRD monitoring.coreos.com before it is enabled.

labels.description: Labels of the ServiceMonitor, for example the label that selects it in the Prometheus resource.

prometheusRule.description: A Prometheus Operator PrometheusRule with the alerts of the server. The rules select the metrics by job (the name of the Service, which the ServiceMonitor of the chart gives to the series) and by the namespace of the release. The cluster needs the CRD monitoring.coreos.com before it is enabled.

labels.description: Labels of the PrometheusRule, for example the label that selects it in the Prometheus resource (ruleSelector).

name.description: The name of a Kubernetes object, a DNS-1123 subdomain.

nameOrEmpty.description: The name of a Kubernetes object, a DNS-1123 subdomain, or empty when the setting is not used.

dnsLabel.description: A DNS label, 1 to 63 characters from lower case letters, digits and "-".

secretKey.description: The key of a Secret, from letters, digits, "-", "_" and ".". It names an entry; it is never the value of an enrollment token.

secretKeyOrEmpty.description: The key of a Secret, as above, or empty when the setting is not used.

hostname.description: A lower case host name, optionally with a leading wildcard label such as *.example.com.

registryHost.description: A registry host with an optional port, for example ghcr.io or registry.example.com:5000. Empty when not used.

cidr.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 network in CIDR notation, for example 169.254.0.0/16.

quantity.description: A Kubernetes quantity, a number or a string such as 500m, 512Mi or 5Gi.

quantityMap.description: Quantities by resource name, for example cpu, memory and ephemeral-storage.

intOrPercent.description: A number of pods or a percentage of the pods, for example 1 or 50%.

stringMap.description: A map from strings to strings. An entry may be null: the values files of the examples switch off an entry of an earlier values file that way, and Helm keeps such a null for a key that values.yaml does not define.

gatewayDuration.description: A duration in the format of the Gateway API, for example 30s or 1h30m.

probeCount.description: A number of seconds or attempts, at least 1.

networkPolicyPeer.description: A source or destination of a NetworkPolicy rule, with exactly one of its selectors.

networkPolicyPort.description: A port of a NetworkPolicy rule.

envVar.description: An environment variable in the format of a Kubernetes container.
